evals.prompt: Refactor the Companion chat screen so polling and send state survive navigation, cancellation does not publish stale results, and the UI remains testable. Keep API/session logic in CompanionKit.
evals.expected_output: A focused SwiftUI implementation plan or patch that uses stable model ownership, value-driven navigation, structured cancellable tasks, actor/main-actor boundaries, stable IDs, injected effects, and accessibility-aware states, while preserving the shared API contract and handing build verification to xcodebuildmcp-cli.

evals.prompt: My SwiftUI list redraws too much when one Companion changes. What should I inspect first?
evals.expected_output: A concise diagnostic that checks state ownership, unstable identity, broad observation, expensive body work, and unnecessary type erasure before proposing measured changes; it does not invent a new design system or run unrelated build steps.

evals.prompt: A slow poll finishes after a newer response, the user enabled Reduce Motion, and Dynamic Type clips the retry action. Fix the SwiftUI edge cases without changing the endpoint.
evals.expected_output: An implementation focused on version/resource guards, cancellation and stale-result suppression, explicit reduced-motion behavior, Dynamic Type-safe layout, accessible labels/identifiers, and tests with injected effects.

evals.prompt: Choose the accent palette and decide whether the iOS product should use a sidebar or tabs.
evals.expected_output: A routing response that sends visual/product direction to design-frontend-dev and ios-product-dev, explains that SwiftUI expert is not the owner of the design register, and avoids prescribing a build or API change.
